prompt:
A single flat sheet of SIX separate game-asset paintings arranged in a strict 3-column by 2-row grid, evenly spaced, each object fully inside its own cell with clear empty margin around it and no object touching or overlapping another. Read the cells left to right, top row first.

STYLE, and this is the most important instruction: hand-painted 2D storybook nautical illustration, exactly matching the reference images supplied. Confident dark warm-brown ink linework of varying weight drawn over soft watercolour washes, with visible paper grain and brush texture inside the shapes. Warm timber browns, cream plaster, muted slate-blue and soft sage accents. Slightly wonky hand-drawn geometry, no ruler-straight edges. This is a PAINTING, not a render: no 3D shading, no airbrush gradients, no baked ambient occlusion, no glossy specular highlights, no plastic sheen.

CAMERA, identical for all six cells: three-quarter view from slightly above, each object rotated about thirty degrees so its front and its left-hand side are both visible, viewed from roughly twenty-five degrees above the ground line. Every object sits at the same angle, the same orientation and the same apparent scale within its cell, so the six read as one set drawn the same way, and so that they match the crew hall buildings drawn in the same style. The base of each object sits on an implied ground line at the same height in every cell.

LIGHT, identical for all six: a single warm sun from the upper left, cool soft fill from the upper right, warm interior light glowing through any lit window.

The six are one provision store upgraded five times: the SAME crew larder, growing from scraps to a full hold. Each cell is a small tight GROUP of crates, casks and food, not a building, and the group keeps its family so the change reads as the same store improved.

Cell 1: a single small plank crate with a dark loaf of bread and a dented tin mug on the lid, and a slumped hessian sack leaning against it.

Cell 2: two stacked crates and a small oak barrel, a wheel of yellow cheese on top, and a rope of onions hanging over the side.

Cell 3: a stack of crates with a brass-hooped barrel beside them, salted fish strung on a line above, and a cured ham hanging from a hook.

Cell 4: a well-stocked larder stack of crates with a hanging lantern, two casks, and a bunch of dried herbs tied above.

Cell 5: a brass-bound chest open on a stack of crates, tall wine casks, a crate of citrus fruit, and cured meat hanging above.

Cell 6: a monumental store: a great iron-bound chest, tall dark casks stacked two high, a fat whale-oil jar, and crates piled high under a lashed canvas cover.

ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT. Do not write the name of any building. Do not put a caption, a label, a title or a number under, over or beside any cell. There is no writing anywhere on this sheet.

ABSOLUTELY NO SUN AND NO GLOW. Do not draw the light source. Do not draw a sun, a moon, a halo, a lens flare, a glow, a radial gradient or any bright disc in any cell. The light comes from off the sheet and is only visible in how the buildings are lit.

BACKGROUND: every cell sits on the SAME FLAT PURE MAGENTA field, RGB 255 0 255, edge to edge across the whole sheet. No ground, no grass, no water, no scenery, no cast shadow on the magenta, no cell borders, no frames, no grid lines, no labels, no text, no numbers, no watermark. The magenta must be completely flat and uniform everywhere the buildings are not.
